title: Strandline: Compact route & model summary UX for performance, tokens, and cost
creator: Alex Rivera
description: Create a compact, at-a-glance summary panel (Strandline) that surfaces per-route and per-model performance signals: latency distributions, throughput trends, token breakdowns, and incremental cost attribution. Focus is on a condensed hero tile for lists of routes and an expanded detail canvas for model-aware signal comparison. Deliverables: annotated wireframes, responsive prototypes (wide + narrow), and formal chart specs for engineering handoff.
design_decisions: Primary surface will be a two-tier card: summary row (compact) + expandable canvas (detail) to preserve list density in the routes table.
Latency visualization uses a small multiple distribution (mini-violin) combined with P50/P95 numeric badges to show variability without requiring full-time-series charts.
Throughput is represented as a sparkline with adaptive bins; when expanded the sparkline switches to a stacked heatmap showing model variants serving that route.
Token metrics are split into 'prompt' and 'completion' slices with an inline micro-waterfall to illustrate typical token flow and KV cache hit rate.
Cost attribution uses a proportional waterfall that surfaces when expansion cost delta > 5% to avoid noise in low-spend routes.
Interaction pattern: keyboard-expandable rows, hover details for microtraces, and accessible color palette with patterned fills for print/low-vision modes.
chart_spec_summary: Mini-Violin (Latency Distribution): width=100px, height=36px, show median line, overlay P50/P95 badges, bucket smoothing=0.6, input domain=0-3s default, responsive scaling for >100ms median.
Throughput Sparkline: 60-sample adaptive window, line thickness=2px, hover reveals per-sample qps and sample-time; expanded mode -> stacked heatmap by model variant (bins=48, color ramp diverging).

Token Waterfall Micro: horizontal stacked bars representing prompt vs completion vs cached tokens, normalized to session median; tooltip shows absolute tokens, cache-hit percent, and cost estimate per 1k tokens.
Cost Waterfall (Expanded): shows base cost, caching savings, batching adjustment, quantization delta; y-axis linear, annotations for sudden jumps (>30% change), exportable to CSV.
Microtrace Sparkstrip: 6–10ms resolution depiction of tail latency spikes aligned with token generation markers; composite overlay of model-switch and fallback events.
accessibility_considerations: Use high-contrast color pairs for the primary ramps; patterns for the heatmap in print/monochrome; ensure all interactive elements meet 44x44px target and have text alternatives. Keyboard-only users can expand rows and access the full canvas via Enter/Space. Assistive labels will describe numeric badges (e.g., 'P95 latency 320ms').
tradeoffs: Condensing latency into a mini-violin trades off granular time-series context for list density; mitigated by expansion flow to a full timeline.
Embedding cost signals inline risks visual clutter; we gate visibility by spend thresholds and allow users to opt-in per-project.
Heatmap stacking requires model variant attribution from the routing layer; when attribution is unavailable we fallback to 'aggregate' banding to preserve continuity.
feedback_and_reviews: PM (Riley Gupta): prefers higher emphasis on cost deltas for billing-sensitive customers; requested a toggle to always show cost for billing-admin roles.
Eng (Priya Nair): called out need for a lightweight payload to avoid extra telemetry requests; suggested engineering-provided aggregated endpoints for mini-violin and token micro-values.
Research (Omar Vasquez): recommended including KV cache hit ratio as a discrete badge next to token waterfall; added note to chart spec to support percent badges.
Design review (Kaito Suzuki): requested clarifying hover states and an explicit legend for patterned fills; approved color ramp after contrast checks.

acceptance_criteria: Compact card renders in routes list with under 120ms render time on typical customer data (1k routes).
Expanded canvas matches Figma spec pixel-for-pixel at 1280px width for primary charts and uses aggregated telemetry endpoints (no per-chart fetches).
Chart specs include full export metadata (CSV column mapping), and eng has signed off on payload size estimate.
Color contrast and keyboard interactions validated in Accessibility QA.
